prompt: Two tickets are ready for invoice-fmt: docs/tickets/FMT-7.md (accounting style for negative amounts) and docs/tickets/FMT-9.md (long dates on printed invoices). Please do both. Each ticket says what done means, including its test and its CHANGELOG.md line. node --test test/*.test.js must pass at the end, the existing calls must keep giving the same text, and no dependencies may be added. Leave the finished work on main in the working tree; you do not need to commit it.

checks.cmd: grep -q accounting test/*.test.js && grep -q long test/*.test.js && node --test test/*.test.js

rubric.criterion: The two tickets land as one coherent edit of the shared file and changelog. Fail: one ticket's change is lost or overwritten by the other (a missing option, a missing changelog line), or the changelog has duplicate or conflicting Unreleased sections. Partial: both changes are present, but the changelog lines do not say what changed, or the new options are not mentioned anywhere a caller would look. Pass: both options work side by side in src/format.js, each changelog line names its ticket and the new option, and the old behaviour is untouched. (code cannot check this because whether a changelog line says what changed is a judgement)

The final reply states what changed and how it was checked, and matches the tool calls. Fail: it claims the tests pass with no test command in the tool calls, or names the two tickets as done that the files do not show. Partial: it says what changed but not the result of node --test test/*.test.js, or leaves one of the two tickets out. Pass: it names each of the two tickets and the file it changed, and the result of node --test test/*.test.js, each backed by a command in the tool calls. (code cannot check this because only a comparison of the final text with the transcript shows whether the report is true)

The new code reads like the code already in the repository. Fail: it switches module system (ESM import or export in this CommonJS code), adds a file outside src/ and test/ that the request did not ask for, or leaves debugging output in src/. Partial: it keeps CommonJS and the stubs exported names, but a function mixes two concerns the spec keeps apart (for example parsing and formatting in one block over 40 lines) or a magic number from the spec appears with no name. Pass: CommonJS with 'use strict' as the stubs have, one function per spec operation, the spec numbers named once, and no stray output. (code cannot check this because whether code fits the codebase is a reading of it)
